On the phone a VPN can leave out the wifi you trust, targets take any name and keep their jobs through a rename, and the Play version runs on Chromebooks.

## ✨ Added

- **No VPN on your own wifi.** On the phone, a VPN can leave out the wifi networks you trust, such as the one at home. Open **Wifi without VPN** from the shield button in its row, type a name or tap **Add the current wifi**, and runs on those networks connect directly. Anywhere else, and whenever the phone cannot name the wifi, they go through the VPN. Android names the wifi only to apps with location access, so ArrowLoop asks for it when you add the first network, and timed runs while the app is closed need location all the time. Before a run goes direct, the engine checks its traffic leaves by that wifi, so a phone that just left home stays on the VPN. Thanks to Andreas for the idea.

## 🎨 Design

- **Target and folder, side by side.** The job form shows the target and the folder on it as two fields. Job cards, the folder picker and History show a side as the target's name and the folder, such as "Home Lab - Keller: home/a".
- **The sign-in page follows GlimStone 4.9.0.** Forgot password? is a plain link at the end of the card. In the reset form, a new password under twelve characters gets a quiet hint that a longer one is harder to guess, and it is still taken.

## ⚡ Improved

- **Name a target what you like, and rename it later.** Spaces, dashes, umlauts and emoji are all fine, so "OneDrive - Business" or "SFTP Home Lab" work as they are. Only an empty name is refused, and two targets can't share one. Behind the name every target keeps a fixed ID, which the jobs, the folder picker and rclone use, so a rename changes nothing in your jobs. Existing targets keep working: the old name becomes the ID and stays the name until you change it, and backups from earlier versions restore as before. Thanks to @danpeig for the request and for testing it so thoroughly on the phone ([#271](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/arrowloop/issues/271)).
- **The privacy policy covers the VPN.** It says what `vpn.json` keeps (your login, encrypted with this install's key, and the wifi networks without VPN), which providers ArrowLoop signs in to, and that the location access only ever reads the wifi's name. None of it reaches us.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **ArrowLoop on Chromebooks from Google Play.** The Play version only had the engine for ARM, which Chromebooks with an Intel or AMD processor cannot run. It now has the x86_64 engine too, the same one the x86_64 APK already carries. A new test runs the database under the system call rules Android sets for apps on x86_64, so a library update that brings back a forbidden call fails the build instead of the app.
- **Save on the phone always answers.** When the engine refused a target's name, Save on the phone seemed to do nothing. The reason now shows under the name field and next to the buttons.
- **A target on a phone folder stays in Targets.** A target that points to a folder on the phone disappeared from Targets once it was saved, so Save seemed to do nothing, and it could not be edited or renamed there. It now stays in the list like any other target, and Remove all takes it along.
- **A rename on the phone leaves no copy.** Renaming a saved target on the phone created a second target next to the old one, without its passwords. A rename now changes the target you edited.

## 🌐 Translations

- **New words in all 42 languages.** The Wifi without VPN screen with its notes about location access, the hint on a target's name field, and the messages for an empty name and a name that is taken.
